acceptance: A job produces per-table checksums and row counts on both platforms and fails on mismatch
dsqgen -LOG output for a pinned seed is compared across platforms for all 99 templates
The result of the first comparison is recorded in this item
context:
Source: DataFrame query parity proposal v3 (item T15). Needs a CI runner; the author could only measure macOS. Informs owner decision D3 in dfparity-t00-owner-decisions. Project owner does NOT accept earlier reviewers' TPC-H claims.

Progress 2026-10-01/02: implemented as PR #2523 (branch feat/tpcds-platform-identity-check, worktree ../BenchBox.wt-tpcds-platform-identity): scripts/tpcds_platform_identity.py (manifest and compare), .github/workflows/tpcds-platform-identity.yml (Ubuntu and macOS manifests, a compare job; daily, on demand and on PRs touching the bundled TPC-DS binaries or this check; not a required check), ledger rows, 12 tests (medium lane); make pr-preflight exit 0. FIRST COMPARISON (TESTED, hosted run 36960455608 on the PR's own workflow): darwin-arm64 against linux-x86_64: 25 tables, 99 queries, 0 differences. That is per-table row count and sha256 of the raw dsdgen output at SF 0.01, the dsqgen -LOG values for all 99 templates at seed 7, and the sha256 of the rendered SQL: identical on both platforms. Finding while building it: dbgen_version holds the generation date and time and differs between two runs of the same binary, so only its row count is compared. IMPLICATIONS: (1) for D3, the bundled dsqgen -LOG output is identical on the two platforms tested, so a runtime -LOG approach is not undermined by cross-platform drift on those; darwin-x86_64, linux-arm64 and Windows binaries are NOT checked (no runners of those architectures in the matrix; Windows has a known transient Q46 cities failure and CRLF would change the data checksums). (2) cross-platform data or parameter differences are an unlikely explanation for the Q70 divergence an automated review reported on another machine; library or version differences (for example float behavior) remain candidates. Remaining: review follow-up, merge, then finish. Windows and the other architectures are a follow-up for the owner (design question: schedule only, or also on PRs).
description: Automated Codex reviews twice reported a Q70 divergence that did not reproduce on the author's macOS machine, and bundled dsqgen/dsdgen binaries differ per platform (benchbox/_binaries/tpc-ds/<platform>/). Add a CI job (or scheduled lane) that generates data at a small scale on Linux and macOS runners, records a per-table manifest checksum and row counts, and compares dsqgen -LOG output for a fixed seed across platforms. Until this exists, no scale or timing choice is trustworthy across platforms.
